description: We are a team of students interested in technology, software development, AI, data visualization, and multimedia. For The Earth Information Jukebox challenge, we aim to create an interactive project that transforms Earth data into an engaging audio experience. We welcome members with skills in coding, UI/UX, Earth science, design, audio, research, or storytelling.
summary:
AURA-EARTH is an interactive, browser-native sonification jukebox that translates visual data frames from NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) into real-time, spatialized soundscapes. While NASA’s EIC captures critical planetary changes from marine heatwaves to tropical precipitation and wildfire clusters relying purely on visual media limits accessibility for blind and low-vision audiences.

Built with HTML5 Canvas, the Web Audio API, and the Web Speech API, AURA-EARTH scans EIC visualization frames column by column, converting calibrated color anomalies into musical harmonies mapped to a C-Lydian scale. Longitude maps smoothly across stereo panning (West to East), while latitude maps to pitch (South to North), enabling listeners to locate climate events by ear. Users can upload multi frame NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) image sequences, scrub longitudes via keyboard arrows, audition four calibrated intensity reference tones, and trigger spoken telemetry descriptions making Earth science multi-sensory, accessible, and engaging.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

AURA-EARTH ("Acoustic Unified Real-time Analyzer for Earth") is a zero-dependency web application that transforms NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) and Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) equirectangular frames into spatialized, harmonic soundscapes in real time:

1. Computer Vision Pixel & Colorbar Extraction: Using the HTML5 Canvas 2D API (`getImageData`), an offscreen buffer scans EIC imagery from West to East (180°W to 180°E). Each vertical longitude slice is divided into 16 latitude bands (from 90°S to 90°N).

2. Scientific Dataset Transfer Functions: Users select from four calibrated NASA SVS dataset profiles—Sea Surface Temperature Anomaly (SVS ID 5176), Global Precipitation GPM Constellation (SVS ID 4285), Active Fires VIIRS (SVS ID 5113), and Perpetual Ocean 2 Western Boundary Currents (SVS ID 5425). Each profile decodes dataset-specific RGB colorbar values into normalized anomaly intensities (0% to 100%).

3. Multi-Frame Time-Series Sequencer & Temporal Delta (Δ): Users can upload sequential NASA SVS image frames (`.png`/`.jpg`) or load a calibrated 4-frame time-series sequence. As the scanline completes each global or regional pass, it advances through the time series and computes the frame-to-frame pixel Delta (Δ) to modulate filter resonance and telemetry readouts.

4. Spatial & Harmonic Web Audio Synthesis: Rather than mapping raw data to harsh noise, AURA-EARTH quantizes the 16 latitude bands to a 16-note C-Lydian musical scale (`C3` 130.81 Hz at the South Pole up to `D5` 587.33 Hz at the North Pole). Longitude maps continuously to a Web Audio `StereoPannerNode` (`-1.0` Left Ear to `+1.0` Right Ear). The top 3 active latitude bands per column are synthesized polyphonically (`sine` for baseline/moderate, `triangle` for elevated, and `sawtooth` for extreme anomalies) over a subtle `C2` (`65.41 Hz`) planetary equilibrium drone.

ACCESSIBILITY, CREATIVITY & DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS

- 4-Level Calibrated Audio Legend (Keys 1–4): Before listening to a complex visualization, blind and low-vision users can press keys `1` through `4` to audition calibrated reference tones for Baseline (0–25%, C3 Sine), Moderate (26–50%, G3 Sine), Elevated (51–75%, E4 Triangle), and Extreme (76–100%, B4 Sawtooth) anomalies.

- Spoken Telemetry Narration (Key N): Powered by the W3C Web Speech API (`speechSynthesis`), pressing `N` speaks a clear natural-language report of the active NASA dataset, data mode, longitude, stereo pan position, peak anomaly percentage, and musical pitch.

- Keyboard-First Navigation & Regional Focus (Key W): Users can play/pause (`Space`), reset (`R`), scrub longitudes step-by-step (`ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`), and press `W` to focus the sweep specifically on the Western Pacific, Philippine Sea, and Bicol Region (`120°E–140°E, 5°N–20°N`) with expanded stereo imaging.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

AURA-EARTH empowers blind and low-vision students, educators, museum visitors, and coastal communities in typhoon-prone regions like Bicol and the Western Pacific to experience NASA Earth science independently. Because it runs 100% client-side in any standard web browser and includes a built-in `.webm` audio recorder, teachers and science communicators can immediately generate and export accessible climate sonifications without installing specialized software.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & TECHNOLOGIES USED

- Pure HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla ES6+ JavaScript (zero external npm dependencies)

- HTML5 Canvas 2D Context API (`getImageData` pixel extraction & real-time spectrum/waveform visualization)

- W3C Web Audio API (`AudioContext`, `OscillatorNode`, `StereoPannerNode`, `BiquadFilterNode`, `AnalyserNode`, `MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode`)

- W3C MediaStream Recording API (`MediaRecorder` for live `.webm` audio export)

- W3C Web Speech API (`speechSynthesis` & `SpeechSynthesisUtterance`)

- WCAG 2.1 High-Contrast Dark UI with ARIA live regions (`aria-live="assertive"`)

SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) DISCLOSURE

Generative AI (Google Gemini / Antigravity) was used during the hackathon window to assist with brainstorming the spatial audio mapping architecture, scaffolding HTML/CSS/JavaScript code, and structuring documentation. All scientific visual data frames come from NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) or transparent procedural calibration canvases, and all audio is synthesized mathematically in real time via Web Audio API oscillators (zero AI-generated images, video, or audio files are used).
